faq: Do I need a paid app for a cart drawer?
Sometimes. Some themes include a drawer already. If your theme does not, we use the cheapest reliable option and tell you the monthly cost before installing anything.
Will the cart work with my discount and shipping rules?
Yes. We test with your real discount codes and shipping rates, and we note anything that behaves differently in the drawer from the full cart page.
Can the add-on suggestions be chosen by hand?
Yes. You tell us your best pairings, such as a case with a phone or a cream with a brush, and we set them up. Automatic suggestions are used only where you want them.
Does this slow my store down?
We keep the code light and check page speed before and after. If an app adds too much weight, we tell you and choose a lighter route.

desc:
Cart drawer, upsell and shipping bar setup turns the cart into a clear, helpful step instead of a place where shoppers give up. Ecom Swift LLC builds these cart features in your own store and tests them with real orders before they go live.

## Why the cart is where sales are decided

The cart is the moment a shopper stops browsing and starts weighing the cost. Shipping, total price, discount codes and doubts about the purchase all arrive together. If the cart is cluttered, slow or confusing on a phone, the shopper has an easy reason to close the tab.

Many stores treat the cart as a plain list of items. A better cart answers the questions in the shopper's head: what will I pay, when will it arrive, can I use my code, and is there anything I forgot?

## What is a cart drawer?

A cart drawer is a panel that slides in from the side when a shopper adds an item, instead of sending them to a separate cart page. The shopper stays on the product or collection they were browsing, sees what is in the cart and can continue shopping or go to checkout with one tap.

This keeps momentum. A page reload after every add to cart breaks the browsing flow, especially on a phone with a weaker connection.

## How cart changes affect order value and completion

Each part of the cart does a specific job. A free shipping bar shows how much more a shopper needs to add to qualify, which gives a concrete reason to add one more item. A well chosen add-on suggestion offers something that fits what is already in the cart. A visible checkout button means the shopper never has to hunt for the next step.

These changes work by removing friction and offering relevant choices at the moment of decision. They do not work by pressure. An add-on that has nothing to do with the cart looks like clutter and can reduce trust.

## What a good cart includes

- A slide-out drawer or a clean cart page that loads quickly on mobile.
- Clear item rows with image, name, variant, price and quantity.
- Quantity buttons and a remove link that are easy to tap with a thumb.
- A free shipping progress message tied to your real shipping rules.
- One to three add-on suggestions chosen for the items in the cart.
- A discount code field that is visible but not distracting.
- A running subtotal and an estimated delivery message.
- A checkout button that stays in view as the cart grows.
- Optional gift note or gift wrap choices where they suit your products.
- Cart events recorded in analytics, so you can see how shoppers use the cart.

## How we set up your cart

We start by using your cart as a shopper would, on several phone sizes and on desktop, and note every point of friction. Then we build the changes in your own theme, working on a copy where that is possible. We connect the free shipping bar to your actual shipping threshold, so it never promises something your checkout does not deliver.

For add-ons, we choose suggestions together with you, either by hand for your best sellers or by simple rules for larger catalogs. We place a test order for each change, check discount codes and shipping rules, and write down what we set so you can adjust it later.

The Basic package tidies the cart layout, adds the free shipping message and checks the mobile view. The Standard package adds a cart drawer, add-on suggestions, a well placed code field and a delivery message. The Premium package adds rules for more products, gift options, trust messages, analytics events and handover notes. Add-ons let you extend the rules or add a mini cart on product pages.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Base the shipping bar on a threshold you can afford.
- Offer add-ons that match what is in the cart.
- Keep the checkout button visible at all times.
- Test the cart with a discount code and a shipping change.
- Look at the cart on a small phone before you approve it.

**Avoid:**
- Showing five or more suggestions that push the checkout button out of view.
- Promising free shipping that the checkout does not apply.
- Hiding the discount code field so shoppers leave to search for codes.
- Adding pop-ups over the cart.
- Installing several cart apps that compete with each other.

## Who this is for

This service suits a store that gets plenty of add to cart clicks but fewer completed orders, an owner who wants to raise average order value without discounting everything, and a shop whose cart looks fine on desktop but feels cramped on phones.

## What we need from you

Send us your free shipping rule, any products you want suggested as add-ons and any discount rules you use. Access can be given as a collaborator, staff or developer user, and we never ask for your password. Once you order, a short checklist arrives and we confirm the plan before building.
